auditor_case.summary: WO25-02469 bills ₹16,754 for a 3.4 sqm mastic-asphalt patch on Sion Trombay Road (RD0235) one day after WO25-01483 recorded the same work on the same road, by the same contractor, for nearly the same amount — and RD0235 is still within its Defect Liability Period.
evidence: WO25-02469 has no linked complaint. WO25-01483 (linked to complaint BMC25-003870) matches it on road, work type, repair method and area (3.4 sqm each), completed 1 day apart, with a 2.49% cost difference (₹16,754 vs ₹17,181).
RD0235 is under DLP until 2027-02-14, yet BMC was billed for both repairs. The original DLP contractor is not identified in the records.
WO25-02469 has no before photo, no after photo and no measurement book entry; only the engineer completion certificate is present.

The Marathi complaint BMC25-003869 describes an open drain cover but was categorised as a pothole and closed as a duplicate of BMC25-003870, which was filed 22 minutes later. No drain-cover work order exists.

BMC25-004202 (Hinglish, 2025-08-23) reports the same pothole reopening, and road-condition accidents ACC25-0341 and ACC25-0397 were recorded after completion. This later road-condition signal conflicts with the completion record and supports physical verification; it does not prove causation.

possible_legitimate_context: Both bills are within the normal rate range (1.07× and 1.10× of the RC03 rate), so this is not a pricing concern.
A busy arterial road can have two separate defects of similar size; the records cannot show whether WO25-02469 covers a different spot from WO25-01483.

RD0235 carries 3,723 peak-hour vehicles with congestion 8.3/10 and sits 180 m from flood hotspot FH035; heavy rain was recorded in M/E on 2025-08-07 and 2025-08-18/19, which can break fresh patches quickly.
The contractor on these work orders is not shown to be the DLP warranty holder; it may have been asked to carry out urgent work that the original DLP contractor did not.
limitations: The original DLP contractor and contract are not in the dataset.
Photograph fields are Y/N flags only; no images were reviewed.
Accident records share the road and date range only and cannot establish causation.

response.reasoning: DLP review takes precedence: while RD0235 is under DLP, whether BMC should pay at all depends on who holds the warranty, which only the Ward Warranty Desk can establish. The duplicate-like record is unresolved and is carried into the evidence request rather than ignored.
evidence_required: Original DLP contract and identity of the warranty holder (Ward Warranty Desk)
Confirmation whether the defect falls within DLP scope
Geotagged before/after photographs for WO25-02469 and WO25-01483
Separate-defect justification: why WO25-02469 represents separate work from WO25-01483
response.citizen_explanation: Sion Trombay Road is still under a repair guarantee. Two similar repair bills were recorded a day apart, so before BMC pays, the ward's warranty desk will check who is responsible and ask for photos and measurements. This is a check, not an accusation.
response.officer_brief: Route WO25-02469 (₹16,754) to the Ward Warranty Desk. Ask for the DLP contract, geotagged photos for both orders, the measurement book entry and a separate-work justification. Do not attribute the DLP issue to Tidewater Paving until ownership is known.
